stem.text: In the circuit shown, XY is a length $L$ of uniform resistance wire. A potential difference is applied across XY. $\text{R}_1$ and $\text{R}_2$ are unknown resistors. J is a sliding contact that joins the junction of $\text{R}_1$ and $\text{R}_2$ to points on XY through a lamp S.

stem.alt: Circuit with a wire XY labelled L, a sliding contact J, a lamp labelled S, resistors labelled R1 and R2, and terminals marked minus and plus. An arrow labelled x is drawn along the wire from X.

stem.text: J is moved along XY to a point at which the lamp is off. This point is at a distance $x$ from X.
The potential difference across $\text{R}_1$ is $V_1$ and the potential difference across $\text{R}_2$ is $V_2$.
What is the value of the ratio $\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}$?
